I will keep to the way I know best here in Quzhou: winter wheat first, then summer maize on the same land. Our place on the North China Plain suits this two-crop pattern, and at my age I will not chase complicated crops that need more labor or more market risk. Wheat gives me a steady harvest and uses the winter-spring season well, and maize follows right after wheat so the land does not sit idle. I will use improved seed, not the most expensive fancy option, because I want stable emergence and stable yield. For field work, I will keep fertilizer moderate, water when the crop most needs it, and spray only as much as needed to control the usual diseases, insects, and weeds. For tillage, I will keep it practical: rotary tillage before sowing maize, while the wheat field management stays with the normal local practice already set from last autumn. I will aim for solid yield, lower trouble, and work that I can still manage steadily myself.
